Factor volatility matrix whose eigenvalues follow vector auto-regressive (VAR) model. Accounts for dynamics of factor volatilities using high-frequency data. Uses penalized optimization with truncation scheme for heavy-tailed observations. Approximate factor model structure imposed on large volatility matrices.

Idiosyncratic volatility matrix whose eigenvalues also follow VAR dynamics. Unlike prior literature that treats idiosyncratic volatility as martingale, FIVAR models both factor and idiosyncratic volatility dynamics. Empirically shown to exhibit strong lag-1 autocorrelations in eigenvalue time series.
MSCI USA Value Weighted Index (replaced prior to 1997/12). Used as long-only factor index representing value factor for regime analysis. ETF ticker: VLUE.
MSCI USA Low Size Index (replaced by MSCI USA Equal Weighted Index prior to 1994/6). ETF ticker: SIZE. Small size factor for regime-based allocation.
MSCI USA Momentum SR Variant Index (replaced by MSCI USA Momentum Index prior to 2002/6). ETF ticker: MTUM. Momentum factor for regime-based allocation.
MSCI USA Sector Neutral Quality Index (replaced by MSCI USA Quality Index prior to 1998/12). ETF ticker: QUAL. Quality factor for regime-based allocation.
MSCI USA Minimum Volatility Index (replaced by MSCI USA Risk Weighted Index prior to 1994/6). ETF ticker: USMV. Low volatility factor for regime-based allocation.
Russell 1000 Growth Index. ETF ticker: IWF. Growth factor for regime-based factor allocation.

Diebold-Yilmaz volatility connectedness index measuring spillover effects among stock markets. Quantifies how volatility shocks in one market transmit to others via VAR-based forecast error variance decomposition.

Quant Cycle concept: factor performance is cyclical with predictable phases. Value and momentum factors alternate in dominance. Factor crowding measured by relative valuations and flows. Early cycle favors momentum, late cycle favors value.

Machine learning risk model using k-means clustering to identify statistical risk factors from return covariance/correlation structure. Clusters of correlated stocks form risk factors, replacing traditional PCA-based approaches. Number of clusters determined data-driven.

Regime-conditional expected returns used as investor views in Black-Litterman framework. Prior beliefs from sample means/covariances updated with regime-predicted expected returns. Dynamic allocation adjusts factor index weights based on bull/bear regime inference.

Standard equity factors (value, quality, low risk, momentum, size) analyzed over 1963-2020. Historical perspective showing recent underperformance of value factor is within historical norms. Factor definitions follow standard academic conventions (HML, RMW, CMA, WML, SMB).
factors.source_paper: SSRN-Equity factor investing Historical perspective of recent performance(2020).pdf

factors.factor_name: Dynamic Portfolio Views at Multiple Horizons
factors.definition: Extension of Black-Litterman to incorporate views at multiple investment horizons simultaneously. Views can differ across time horizons, allowing tactical tilts while maintaining strategic allocation.
factors.source_paper: SSRN-Dynamic Portfolio Management with Views at Multiple(2015).pdf

factors.definition: Sharpe ratio adjusted for multiple testing and model selection effects. Provides conservative assessment of risk-adjusted performance, guarding against overstating significance with multiple design choices. Accounts for number of trials, skewness, and kurtosis of returns.

Binary classification of stock excess return direction (positive vs negative) shown to be more important than magnitude prediction for portfolio performance. Comparison of direction vs value prediction models.
AI-driven dual strategy combining behavioral profiling with asset management. Prototype for regime-aware allocation using investor behavioral signals.
Advancing Markowitz optimization using Random Forest to predict expected returns and covariances. ML-based signal replaces traditional estimation for mean-variance optimization inputs.
